title: Arrangers are contained by removing their capability to cause loss, with delay and inconvenience accepted as the price
content:
A.3.4.3.1 defines Arrangers as the specialists who source, negotiate, structure and report on RWAs, and who "manage a restricted function on the Arranged Structure Conduit that allows them to send assets onwards to the predetermined blockchain account of the Arranged Structure." Note how narrow that power is: they can push assets to *one predetermined destination*, not to an address of their choosing.

The containment principle is then stated twice, in strong terms. "Arrangers are generally prohibited from occupying any position where they could cause damage or loss to the Sky Ecosystem, **notwithstanding delays or inconveniences**." And: "After the Arranged Structures are established and assets are allocated, Arrangers must not have the capability to operate or influence the legal and operational structure's asset operations in any manner that could cause significant harm or losses to the stability of USDS."

The operative word is *capability*. The standard is not that Arrangers must behave well, be bonded, or be legally liable — it is that they must be structurally unable to do damage. This is trust-minimization applied to an offchain counterparty, where the usual crypto tools (immutable code, multisigs, timelocks) are unavailable and the substitute is legal-structural design.

The explicit acceptance of "delays or inconveniences" is the load-bearing concession, and it is unusually honest. Removing an operator's discretion necessarily makes the structure slower and clumsier: assets can only move to predetermined destinations, changes need the Agent owner, and opportunistic action is impossible. The Atlas states in advance that this cost is worth paying, which pre-empts the standard argument for granting operational latitude — that the current situation is urgent.

This is also the clause that makes the Arranger role separable from the Asset Manager and Agent-owner roles. The Arranger holds the expertise and the reporting duty; the Agent owner holds the authority; and A.3.4.4 lets the latter replace the former at will precisely because the Arranger's removal cannot destabilize the assets.
description: After a structure is established, Arrangers must not be able to influence asset operations in any way that could cause significant harm
